stories.title: Benjamin Netanyahu promises high-tech entrepreneur Dobronsky AI minister role
stories.simple_summary: A government in Israel is creating a new minister position focused on AI and offering it to a tech entrepreneur.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people in that country — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Apple could help you prove your iPhone photos aren’t deepfakes
stories.simple_summary: Apple is working on a way to prove that photos taken on your iPhone are real and haven't been faked with computer tricks.
stories.why_it_matters: If you take photos on your iPhone, eventually you might be able to prove to others they're genuine — useful if someone doubts your pictures are real.

stories.title: North Carolina Central University opens NC's first artificial intelligence building
stories.simple_summary: A university in North Carolina opened a new building dedicated to studying and teaching AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to students and educators in that area — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: ‘Zoomsday’ hack uncovered using fewer than 20 AI prompts
stories.simple_summary: Someone discovered a serious security problem with Zoom meetings using AI to help find the flaw, and Zoom has now fixed it so attackers can't take over your device.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Zoom, you're now safer because this dangerous hole has been patched.

stories.title: His Start-Up’s Goal: A.I. That Is Trainable and Not Controlled by a Big Company
stories.simple_summary: A new company is trying to create AI tools that people can control themselves instead of relying on big tech companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech companies — nothing you need to act on right now.

stories.title: Why your Amazon order confirmation emails have become so unhelpful
stories.simple_summary: Amazon's order confirmation emails now show vague categories like 'Beauty item' instead of telling you exactly what you bought.
stories.why_it_matters: If you shop on Amazon, your confirmation emails are now less helpful and harder to understand — you may need to log into your account to see what you actually ordered.

stories.title: Spotify will label ‘AI Persona’ profiles and exclude their music from recommendations
stories.simple_summary: Spotify is labeling fake AI-created artists and will stop recommending their music to you automatically.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Spotify, you're less likely to accidentally hear music from computer-made artists, which some people prefer.

stories.title: Spotify says it won’t recommend music from ‘AI Personas’
stories.simple_summary: Spotify will mark artists that are AI-generated rather than real people and won't suggest their songs in playlists.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Spotify, you'll see which artists are real people and which are computer-created, giving you more control over what you listen to.

stories.title: Claude will apply invisible watermarks to AI text and images
stories.simple_summary: Claude, an AI writing tool, will add hidden digital marks to text and images it creates so people can tell it came from AI.
stories.why_it_matters: If someone shows you writing or pictures online, there may eventually be a way to check if an AI made them — useful for spotting fakes.

stories.title: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic (the company behind Claude AI) will add hidden identification marks to text it generates so you can prove it came from their AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This is similar to other AI watermarking efforts — mostly a technical change for experts right now.

stories.title: Is the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Bubble About to Pop? Investors Who Make This 1 Move Will Come Out on Top, According to History.
stories.simple_summary: An investment advice article asks whether AI companies' stock prices might crash soon.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to stock investors — nothing you need to act on unless you own AI company stocks.

stories.title: The AI takeover of mathematics has begun
stories.simple_summary: Mathematicians are learning to use AI to solve hard math problems much faster than they could before, which is changing how their field works.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to scientists and researchers — nothing you need to act on, though AI is becoming useful in more serious professional fields.
